sources_considered.why: Primary documentation of Bing's search grounding. It does not report the required reversal-task comparison.
Original paper defines the task and distinguishes learned-fact reversal from in-context inference.
Later version also concerns other models; the original version is sufficient to establish the scope.

evidence_items.explanation: Microsoft documents supplementation through search grounding. This neither establishes a controlled benefit on reversal questions nor measures Bing's performance on the synthetic task.

receipt.public_excerpt: The Reversal Curse does not apply for in-context learning.

evidence_items.explanation: The paper distinguishes reversing facts learned during training from reversing facts supplied in context. Its experiments on other models cannot establish the predicted Bing outcome.

unresolved_gaps: No controlled Bing evaluation matching Experiment 1 was located.
No matched comparison isolates Bing's supplementary mechanism as the cause of improvement on known-fact reversal questions.
The available documentation does not establish that Microsoft's grounding mechanism meets Marcus's unspecified definition of neurosymbolic.
The relevant Bing version and a numerical difficulty threshold are unspecified.
